newsitem.title: USA: Babbitt slams bill to boost recreation in refuges.
newsitem.headline: Babbitt slams bill to boost recreation in refuges.

text.p: Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt Thursday said President Clinton should veto a Republican proposal to put fishing and hunting on a par with conservation in wildlife refuges.
Babbitt also objected to a bill that would require Congress to give its approval before any money is taken from a special fund to create a new wildlife refuge.
"I am strongly opposed to both of these bills, and I would be compelled to recommend that the president veto either one," he told a House resources subcommittee hearing.

The House overwhelmingly passed a similar refuge recreation bill last year but the Senate never voted on it. The administration says it would subvert wildlife preservation and trigger lawsuits among competing users of refuges.

"Wildlife conservation is our purpose. ... Compatible recreational uses are benefits that flow from this purpose," Babbitt said. "The bill scrambles the crucial distinction between 'purpose' and 'use' that has been at the heart of the refuge philosophy."

The author of the bill, House Resources Committee Chairman Don Young, said he did not intend to allow a slew of lawsuits among fishermen, hunters, birdwatchers and others who could all claim priority in using wildlife refuges. "We can write in that they can't sue," the Alaska Republican said.

But Babbitt said lawsuits would be unavoidable because the bill would give each group a preferred right to use refuges. "What it does is infuse lawyers and judges ever more deeply into the management of our national wildlife refuge system."

Hunting and fishing is already allowed in more than half of the nation's 510 refuges and Clinton last year issued an executive order that promoted conservation and compatible wildlife-related recreation in refuges.
Representative George Miller, the top Democrat on the House Resources Committee, has introduced a competing bill that would reinforce conservation as the top priority in refuges.
